verdict.rationale: Ghostty documents a built-in AppleScript dictionary for scripting windows, tabs, terminals, layouts and input events, plus Apple Shortcuts support. That gives a real automation surface on macOS, but it is platform-specific. A hands-on probe found the `ghostty` CLI exposes only config and +action commands, with no cross-platform remote-control/IPC for sending commands to or reading output from a running instance. Missing for 10: a cross-platform CLI/IPC remote-control interface, documented state/output querying, Linux scripting beyond systemd single-instance integration, and in-depth AppleScript reference docs or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can script and control the terminal from the command line — open windows, send text, query state — via a documented CLI or IPC interface

citations.quote: AppleScript Automation: Built-in AppleScript dictionary for scripting windows, tabs, terminals, layouts, and input events.
macOS supports AppleScript, Apple Shortcuts (AppIntents), etc.
